paragraphs: The S450 was introduced to the S-Class range in 2017 with the W222 generation, using the then-new M256 3.0-litre inline-six petrol engine. This engine marked a departure from the older M276 V6 that had been used in preceding S-Class variants. The M256 was the first application of a 48-volt mild-hybrid system on a series-production inline-six for Mercedes-Benz, and it remains in production with the current W223 generation S450, where it continues to serve as the entry-level petrol option. Knowing that your S450 uses the M256 regardless of generation helps confirm the correct components and rebuild approach from the outset.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every S450 on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the S450 from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The S450 has used the M256 engine across both of its generations (W222 and W223). While the core engine block and architecture are shared, there are slight revisions between the earlier and later applications. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:
